Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Target allocation & contingency playbook — planning initiation

Hi all,

We need to kick off the annual targets + scenario planning workstream this week so the QBR and executive board receive a clean set of options by the end of May. Attached are two working artifacts to start: a scenarios deck and a cost/SLO assumptions spreadsheet.

High level asks:
- Review the three scenarios (base / downside / upside) and call out any model, infra, or hiring assumptions that materially change unit economics.
- Owners: please volunteer to own one scenario each (scenario write-up + 1 slide impact).
- Timeline proposal: scenario write-ups by Thu 5/20, internal review 5/24, board prep & one-pager 5/28.

Immediate decisions we need at this stage:
1) Finalize headcount ramp assumptions (engineering & infra).
2) Lock the inference cost curve (current baseline in tab 2 of the spreadsheet).
3) Agree on a contingency trigger matrix (what happens at -10% revenue, -25% ARR churn, etc.).

Can people reply with owners + any red flags on the assumptions by EOD Tue 5/17? I pulled procurement (Alec) in to flag any contract/payment timing constraints that would affect committed capacity or reserved GPU purchases.

Thanks — Aisha

--
Aisha Rahman
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
+aisha@redwood.ai

Attachments:
- 2027_planning_scenarios_v1.pdf (pdf, 8 pages)
- SLO_cost_assumptions.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)

Thanks Aisha — I can own the downside scenario. Quick notes after a skim:
- Hiring ramp: recommend modeling two flavors: conservative (slower hiring, delayed FY27 hires until H2) and aggressive (full ramp). That affects both opex runway and time-to-market for paid features.
- Inference cost: include a sensitivity for 5%–15% improvement from Redwood Optimize recommendations; ops can defer some burst capacity in the downside path.

I'll add a short note to the scenario deck with the hiring sketches and upload by Tue.

Jonas
